Let $k$ have any characteristic. \begin{enumerate} \item[(a)] If $B$ is a principally polarized abelian variety of dimension at most $5$, then $2\in\IJ(B)$; if it has dimension $6$, then $6\in\IJ(B)$. \item[(b)] If $A$ is an abelian surface, then $\sJ(A)\mid\gcd(2,\delta(A))$. If $A$ is an abelian threefold, then $\sJ(A)\mid\gcd(6,\delta(A))$. \end{enumerate} In particular an abelian surface with $\delta(A)$ odd, and an abelian threefold with $\gcd(\delta(A),6)=1$, is a direct summand of a product of Jacobians.
For every complex principally polarized abelian variety $A$, \[ \sJ(A)\mid m(A)\mid \sJ(A)^2 . \] Hence $\rad\sJ(A)=\rad m(A)$, and $\sJ(A)=m(A)$ whenever $m(A)$ is squarefree.

Let $A$ be a very general complex principally polarized abelian variety of dimension $g$. \begin{enumerate} \item[(i)] If $g\in\{4,5\}$, then $\sJ(A)=2$. \item[(ii)] If $g=6$, then $\sJ(A)=6$. \item[(iii)] If $g\ge4$, every prime $p\le g/2$ divides $\sJ(A)$, and $\sJ(A)\mid m(A)\mid (g-1)!$. \end{enumerate}

For $n\in\Z$ the following are equivalent: (i) $n\,\psi_A^{-1}=Z_*$ for an integral algebraic $1$-cycle $Z$ on $\widehat A\times A$; (ii) $n\in\IJ(A)$. In particular $\sJ(A)$ is the least positive integer $n$ such that $n\,\psi_A^{-1}$ is induced by an integral algebraic cycle.

Matsusaka; {\cite[Prop.~3.4]{SS}}: Let $(B,\theta)$ be principally polarized of dimension $h$ over $k$. If an integral $1$-cycle on $B$ has numerical class $n\,\theta^{h-1}/(h-1)!$, then $n\in\IJ(B)$.

(a) $\delta(A)=\gcd\{\chi(L):L\text{ ample}\}$. (b) If $L$ is ample and $n\in\IJ(B)$ for every principally polarized $B$ of dimension $\dim A$, then $n\,\chi(L)\in\IJ(A)$; hence $n\,\delta(A)\in\IJ(A)$. (c) If $\dim A\le3$, then $\delta(A)\in\IJ(A)$.
